text:

does: Lists recent motion events from your cameras, so you can see if a strange shape was a person or just leaves that stir in the wind.

people say:

- was anyone at the back gate while I was out

when are the bins collected

is it a recycling week or a general waste week

Kamau came home after a long night shift, took off their shoes and sat down on the sofa. Their feet hurt and the flat was quiet. "Play something calm," they said to the speaker on the shelf. The speaker started a soft piano playlist.

Then Kamau remembered an old song their grandmother used to sing, one about a horse on a hill. They did not know the name, only the tune, so they hummed a few notes. The speaker listened and said it thought the song was called Little Brown Horse. It asked if Kamau wanted to hear it.

"Yes, that one," Kamau said. The speaker played it. After a minute Kamau said, "Volume down." The speaker turned the music lower. Of all the songs that week, it was the most peaceful, and Kamau fell asleep before it ended.

name: report_ride_problem
does: Lets a rider tell the ride company that something went wrong, like a broken seat belt, a driver who did not know the way, or a sock left on the back seat.
inputs: which ride it was, and what went wrong in a few words
people say:
- the driver went to the wrong street
- my seat belt was stuck in that last ride
- I left my jacket in the car I took this morning
- the car was dirty and the driver was rude
- tell the taxi company my ride was awful

Kai was chopping onions at the restaurant when they remembered that their sister's birthday was on Sunday. Their hands smelled of onion and the oven was set to two hundred degrees, so there was no time to stop. Kai picked up the phone with one clean knuckle and typed fast: "gift idea for my sister, she wants to practice potery"

The assistant did not mind the typo. It answered with three ideas: a beginner pottery kit, a set of clay tools and a class voucher. Kai said, "The kit, please," and the assistant added it to a basket in a shop Kai often used. Then it set a reminder for Friday so the gift would come in time.

This year there would be no usual scarf. Kai smiled and went back to the onions.

Someone who just installed a baking app wants the recipe amounts in grams instead of cups.
grams please
show that in grams
how many grams is a cup of flour
switch the recipe from cups to grams
my scale only shows grams, no cups
I'm proud of my banana bread and I want it exactly right, can you give me the amounts by weight?
Change every amount in this recipe to grams.
Could you please give me all the amounts in grams, because my kitchen scale only shows grams and I'd like to bake without guessing?

Tane owned a small hardware shop. On a freezing morning they were unpacking a new drill when the delivery man said the van would come at four.

"Remind me at three thirty to unlock the back door," Tane told the phone. "Don't make it for the whole week, just today. And don't make it a loud alarm. I have customers in the shop."

The phone set one reminder for three thirty today, with a soft sound and no repeat. Tane went back to the boxes and sold two ladders and a bucket of paint before lunch.

At three thirty the phone buzzed gently in Tane's pocket. Tane did not need to look at the clock. They walked to the back, unlocked the door, and the van came in right on time.

Lorenzo stood by the window on a foggy morning, looking at the white street. He could not see the end of the road, and he was bored.

"Excuse me, could you please tell me how many days are left until the first of December?" he asked the tablet. "My mom said we can open the first door of the advent calendar then, and I want to know how long I have to wait."

The assistant looked at today's date and worked out the total. "There are twenty-three days left," it said. "Would you like me to count down for you each morning?"

"Yes, please," said Lorenzo. The assistant said it would tell him the number every day after breakfast. Lorenzo drew a big X on his paper calendar and decided that twenty-three days was not so long after all.

Someone wants their book read out loud from where they stopped, instead of reading it themselves.
read to me
continue the book out loud
pick up where I left off
my eyes are too tired to read tonight
I'm cooking and I can't hold the book, any chance you could read it?
read it in a deep voice, like the old captain, it always makes me laugh
can you read my book out like you read my voicemail messages?

Ruta was home alone and hungry when the kitchen tap began to drip. Drip, drip, drip, all afternoon. Ruta picked up the phone and texted the assistant.

"book a plumber for tomorrow morning pls"

The assistant found a plumber with a free time at nine. Before it could confirm, Ruta typed again.

"wait no not tomorrow. my birthday party is tomorrow night and i need the kitchen clear. make it thursday"

The assistant said, "Of course. I'm moving it from tomorrow to Thursday at nine." It booked the new time and cancelled the old one. Ruta got a message with the plumber's name and a small repair price.

Then Ruta put a bucket under the tap, made a sandwich, and finally stopped feeling hungry.

When you ask your phone for directions, it picks a route and tells you how long the drive will take. The route is for getting somewhere without getting lost. But roads change. A crash, road work or heavy rain can make the trip longer, so the time on the screen can change too.

People change a route in simple ways. They might say, "add a stop at the petrol station" or "avoid the motorway." They might say, "take me the quickest way" or "how long until I get there?" On the map, the pale blue line often shows the road you chose. If you are going to the dentist about a sore tooth, you can ask for the shortest road, because every minute counts.

Rhys sat on a bench in the park, thumbs on the phone. At home, the white panels on the roof were busy in the sunshine. Rhys wished to know how much power they were making, but did not feel like typing a long question.

"solar today," Rhys typed.

The assistant opened the energy app and answered: "Your panels have made nine units so far today. The house has used four. The rest is going back to the grid."

Rhys grinned. That was better than yesterday. Then Rhys typed two more words: "washer now?" The assistant said it was a good time, because the sun was strong, and it started the washing machine at home. Rhys put the phone away and watched a dog chase a ball across the park.

Alejandro was not good with technology, and the phone often confused them. But this week there was a surprise to plan, so they sat down at the kitchen table, next to the freezer full of frozen peas, and spoke slowly to the assistant.

"Please write an invitation for my sister's party on the first of June," Alejandro said. "It is a surprise, so please do not let it leak. Only my family should see it."

The assistant wrote a short invitation with the date, the time and the address. It asked if Alejandro wanted any changes. Alejandro said, "Check the spelling, please." The assistant found one mistake in the word "surprise" and fixed it.

Then it saved the invitation in a folder only Alejandro could open. Alejandro was happy and made a cup of tea.

Kevin drove a delivery truck all day, and by evening their eyes were heavy. They had a gallon of water in the cab, but what they wanted was coffee. It was still an hour to get home.

"Start the coffee machine," Kevin said to the phone on the dashboard. The phone asked if they wanted the usual strength. "Stronger," Kevin said, and the phone sent the message to the machine in the kitchen. It was true that Kevin had not slept much, and they hoped the pot would be ready when they walked in.

One hour later the kitchen smelled wonderful. A hot pot of strong coffee sat waiting. Kevin took off their boots and said, "Pour me a cup." The mug was already on the counter, and Kevin did the pouring.

name: tip_driver
does: Adds a tip to a finished ride, so the driver can earn a little more, and shows it on the ride website.
inputs: which ride it was, and the amount or percent to give
people say:
- leave something extra for the driver
- give my driver five dollars
- tip ten percent for that last ride
- the trip was long and the driver was great, I want to give a bit more
- the driver helped with my bags, I want to say thanks

On a busy morning Emre was packing school bags, finding shoes and looking for car keys all at once. In the car at last, with the children buckled in and safe in the back, Emre spoke to the phone.

"Could you please play my audiobook from where I stopped, and make it a little slower? I'm tired this morning, and I want to follow the story during the drive. I'd like to hear the whole chapter before we get to school."

The assistant found the book, a story about a farmer who tries to sell his old farm, and began the next chapter at the right spot. It set the speed to a slower pace than usual. The children sang in the back, but Emre heard the story and arrived calm.

name: flood_watch
does: Warns you when a river bank near your home may overflow, and tells you what to do, like moving to an upper floor and keeping warm clothes close, even on a sunny day when the rain fell far upstream.
inputs: your address or the name of the river
people say:
- is the river going to flood
- the water is coming up the garden
- should I move my car, the river's high
- is my street in danger of flooding tonight
- any flood warnings near me

Vikram had laundry on the line, a tent on the floor and a trip in the morning. Two nights in the hills with friends, and Vikram had no packing list. Thumbs flying, Vikram typed to the assistant.

"packing list for 2 nights in the hils"

The assistant sent a clear list: tent, sleeping bag, warm socks, a torch, a rain jacket, water, a small stove and some food. It even asked if Vikram wanted to add snacks.

"yes snaks," Vikram typed. The assistant added biscuits, nuts and fruit, and asked about dinner. Vikram said they would cook rice and beans. The assistant noted it. Vikram hoped the meals would be delicious and that they would enjoy the quiet. Then Vikram folded the dry laundry into the bag.

Someone wants the radio on a talk station with the news, not music, while they work in the garden on a gray morning.
news radio
put the news on, not music
I'm cutting the grass and I don't want songs, just talk

I expect there's news on at nine, can you tune in?
anything but music right now

Colin sat in the armchair with a bottle of water, waiting for the football match to start. He pressed a button on the remote by mistake, and the sound went off. It was only a little mistake, but the room felt too quiet.

"Undo that," Colin said to the speaker beside the television. The speaker turned the sound back on, and the happy noise of the crowd filled the room.

After a few minutes Colin wanted to know how his team was doing. "Score, please," he said. The speaker answered, "Your team is winning two to one, and there are twenty minutes left."

Colin smiled, held his water bottle tight and leaned toward the screen.

reading reminder, friday morning

name: which_bin
does: Says which bin an item belongs in, and what to move to a different bin to keep the compost healthy.
inputs: the item, such as an old scarf or a pizza box, and your town
people say:
- can I compost this cardboard
- where does an old jumper go
- is a pizza box recycling
- what do I do with a broken lamp
- does this go in the green bin

Most people have a bedtime and a time to wake up. A phone or a watch can help with both. At night it can dim the screen and remind you that it is time to go to bed. In the morning it wakes you with an alarm, and some watches also keep a short chart of how you slept.

When you look at the chart, a single bad night is nothing to worry about. Many people look at the whole week instead. If you snored or woke up with a dry mouth, some trackers note that too.

People change things with simple words: "wake me at seven," "move my alarm to half past six," "remind me to sleep at ten," or "no alarm on Sunday."

Roya drove a city bus, and at the end of a long shift she was tired but proud. At home there were solar panels on the roof, and a cherry tree in the garden that made good shade for the house. Roya wanted to study how much power the house used.

"Could you please tell me how much power my solar panels made today, and how much the house used?" Roya asked the speaker. "I want to know if it is worth running the washing machine now instead of tonight, because I don't want to pay for extra electricity."

The assistant checked the energy app. It said the panels had made twelve units and the house had used five. Running the washer now would use free power from the sun. Roya started it at once and ate a cherry.

Divya was not good with technology, but the kitchen speaker was friendly and never laughed at her.

On Saturday Divya said, "Set a timer for twenty minutes. I'm going to vacuum the stairs." The speaker answered, "Timer set for twenty minutes."

Then Divya looked at the long stairs and changed her mind. "Wait, no. Make it thirty. The stairs are long."

"No problem," said the speaker. "I've changed the timer to thirty minutes."

Divya vacuumed every step. Under the sofa she found a lost folder of bills she had been looking for all week. When the timer rang she was done, the stairs were tidy and the folder was safe on the table. "Lucky me," said Divya.

Yael had a new job in the city and a new flat, but the flat did not have a single lamp. On the first night Yael asked the phone, "Order a tidy little desk lamp and send it to Maple Street."

The assistant found a white lamp and asked for the address. Yael started to say the number, then stopped. "Sorry, not Maple Street. Maple Avenue. Number twelve."

The assistant changed the address and asked Yael to spell the name of the building. Yael spelled it slowly, letter by letter, and the assistant wrote it down. Then it said, "The lamp will arrive on Thursday. I'll send you a message when it is on its way."

Yael sat on the floor with a sandwich and felt a little more at home.

Remembering birthdays is hard when life is busy. An assistant can keep a list of dates, remind you a week before each one, and help you organize gift ideas. For example, a man might say, "remind me about Dad's birthday," and the assistant will tell him early enough to buy something.

People change these reminders in simple ways. They say, "make it two weeks before," "add my cousin's birthday on the ninth," or "find a gift idea for a friend who likes cooking." A shop might offer a red apron or a good knife. The best gifts are the ones that match what the person enjoys.

Notes are for catching an idea before it disappears. Many people think of things at night, when they are about to sleep, and they prefer to speak a quick voice note instead of typing. Later they can look for the note by a word, like "garden" or "phone number."

If the note is not quite right, they change it. They say, "add one more line to my last note," "read my notes from yesterday," or "delete the note about the plumber." It works well when each note is short and has a clear name. One note about one thing is easier to find than a long note about everything.

Person: Make me a strong coffee and add oat milk, please.
Assistant: Happy to. What size cup would you like?
Person: I'm so tired after my shift. Whatever is biggest.
Assistant: Large it is. Strong, with oat milk. It will be ready in two minutes.
Person: Thanks. I also ordered new beans online. Can you check my email for the tracking number?
Assistant: I'm sorry, I can't open your email. I can set a reminder to check it later if you like.
Person: Okay. Can you repeat that? I almost fell asleep.
Assistant: I can't open your email, but I can remind you at noon.

After a nice walk in the forest, Tharushi was tired. Her knees ached a little from the hill, but she had loved watching the birds. At the car park she could not remember where she had left the car.

"Where did I park?" Tharushi asked her phone. The phone showed a small blue dot. "Your car is in the second row, near the sign," it said.

Tharushi found the car and said, "Warm up the car in ten minutes." Then she looked at her cold hands. "No, five minutes. My knees are cold."

The phone changed the timer. Five minutes later the engine started and the heater began to blow. Tharushi sat in a warm seat and drove home slowly.

Things at home wear out. A tap starts to drip, a filter fills with dust, a chair loses a leg. Fixing small things early is cheaper than fixing big things later.

An assistant can help. It can remind you to change a filter every three months, or put a repair visit in your calendar. A filter that looks gray to its full depth needs changing now.

People use simple words: "remind me to change the filter in March," "book someone to fix the tap," or "put a note on the calendar to look at my favourite chair." If you say what is broken and when you are free, the assistant can find a person to come and fix it.

Javier was not good with technology, and the new phone still looked strange to him. He stood in a noisy kitchen, where the oven fan was roaring, trying to write a recipe card for the butter cake his aunt always made.

"I don't understand how this works," Javier told the phone. "Please write down what I say and check the spelling, and then count how many words there are."

The assistant wrote the recipe as Javier spoke: flour, sugar, eggs and a large piece of butter. It corrected the word "sugar" and counted the words. "Your card has sixty-two words," it said.

Javier laughed with relief. It was easier than he thought, and he saved the card for the whole family.

Ryan was a busy parent with two hungry kids, and dinner was almost ready. Outside, the robot mower had stopped halfway across the lawn. Ryan went to the door and saw that it had hit the wire at the edge of the garden.

"Mower, go back to the base and start again tomorrow," Ryan said to the phone. Then Ryan added, "And cut the grass half an inch shorter next time. It was too long last week."

The assistant sent the mower home to charge and set the new height. It said the mower had learned the shape of the lawn and would not touch the flower bed again.

Ryan went back inside. The kids were waiting and the soup was ready.

Ayita parked the red car outside school and dug through the bag for the parking ticket. It was in the bottom, under a sandwich. The meter said the time would end at eight, but tomorrow Ayita would need the spot all day.

"remind me to move my car tomorrow at seven," Ayita typed.

The assistant set the reminder. Then Ayita took a photo of the ticket and asked it to upload the photo to the parking app, so there was proof of payment. The assistant did that and said, "You have one hour and ten minutes left on this ticket."

Ayita thanked it and ran into school. Tomorrow at seven the phone would buzz, and the car would be moved.

Many families keep a few board games in the cupboard. The games are for fun, but they also need a few helpers. Someone keeps the scores, someone looks up a rule, and a timer makes each turn fair. Players race downstairs to join, and the scores climb as the evening goes on.

An assistant can do some of this. People say, "set a two minute timer," "add five points for my team," or "what is the rule for a draw?" In a guessing game, one player might hide a melon in a picture, and the others have to find it before the time runs out. When the game is over, someone says, "who won?" and the assistant reads out the final scores.

Time management is a way to use the day well. Many people work in short blocks, such as twenty-five minutes of focus and then a five minute break. A focus timer keeps the time for you. During the break you stand up, drink water, or sit by the fireplace.

This is a healthy habit, and you can train yourself to do it. People change the plan with simple words: "start a focus timer for twenty-five minutes," "make my break ten minutes today," "stop the timer," or "remind me to stretch at three." After a few weeks, many people say they get more done and feel less tired.

Yan was not good with technology. Last week Yan read in the newspaper about a new noodle shop, and tonight Yan stood in front of the empty fridge.

"There is nothing in my fridge, and my stomach is making noise," Yan said to the speaker.

The speaker understood. It said, "I can find a restaurant. Would you like noodles?" Yan said yes. The speaker found the noodle shop and said it was open until ten.

Then Yan thought of something. "Is it loud there? I can't sleep after loud places." The speaker checked the reviews. "People say it is quiet in the afternoon, but loud at night. Would you like a table at five?"

"Yes, please," said Yan, and the speaker booked it.

workout plan

I need a new routine

what should I do today for my legs
plan my week of workouts, one step at a time

Moshe was at his desk and the clock said noon. He was watching his weight, so he wanted something light. He did not feel like opening the app and picking things by hand. Usually he did everything manual, but today he spoke to his phone.

"Order salad," Moshe said.

The assistant looked at his usual place and ordered a green salad with chicken. It said the food would arrive in twenty minutes. Moshe frowned at the screen.

"Change dressing," he said.

The assistant asked which one. Moshe chose lemon and oil, and the assistant fixed the order. Ten minutes later it told him the courier was nearby. Moshe tidied his desk and waited by the lift.

School and homework have a simple shape. Each subject gives assignments, and each assignment has a due date. A student needs to know what is due next, and how much time there is. An assistant can keep that list and show it when asked.

Students change the list with plain words: "add maths homework for Friday," "move my essay to Monday," "what is due next?" or "remind me to study at four." If a student likes one field of study best, such as science, they can ask for those assignments first. Parents sometimes use the same list to see how the week is going.
